decisions.reason: As a core hardware product very close to the firm's established marking systems, it likely benefits from existing technology, service and sales channels, so the option value of keeping it exceeds the pruning case.
This software module appears somewhat niche, but it extends the firm's digital inline printing portfolio at low ongoing cost, so management would likely keep it unless demand proves clearly weak.
An inkjet coder for non-absorbent surfaces fits directly with the firm's core applications and broad customer base, making continued market presence more attractive than withdrawal.

The decoding app is more peripheral than the equipment products and may require upkeep without large direct revenues, but its low cost and relevance to traceability still make retention slightly more likely.
Inline code verification is strongly aligned with the firm's stated move toward serialization and end-to-end traceability, so management would usually continue supporting it.
Print layout design software complements installed printers and supports the one-stop solution logic, while being relatively inexpensive to maintain compared with dropping it.
